name: FFR 1204.3570 Sec. I: A_tau meant as the self-adjoint (Friedrichs) extension; essential self-adjointness 'not fully resolved'

published_statement: FFR 1204.3570 p. 2, verbatim: 'Throughout this paper, all quadratic operators are understood to be normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state. However, the smeared normal ordered operators are defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain in the Hilbert space (assuming a real-valued smearing function) and it is possible that there is more than one way of extending them to provide self-adjoint operators [39]. The operators of greatest interest to us are bounded from below on account of quantum inequalities (see Sect. II A) and so there is a distinguished Friedrichs extension (see Ref. [17], Theorem X.23), whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind when we discuss the probability distribution of individual measurements of the smeared operator in the vacuum state. The question of whether there is more than one self-adjoint extension, i.e., whether the normal ordered expressions fail to be essentially self-adjoint, is nontrivial and not fully resolved. Recent results (not, however, immediately applicable to our situation) and references may be found in Ref. [18]. If there are distinct self-adjoint extensions, their corresponding probability distributions will all share the same moments in the vacuum state.' Footnote [39]: 'The existence of at least one self-adjoint extension is guaranteed on general grounds because the operators commute with complex conjugation of the n-particle wavefunctions in Fock space.' Kind: a DEFINITION (a choice of self-adjoint realisation) resting on a THEOREM (Friedrichs: a semibounded densely defined symmetric operator has a self-adjoint extension with the same lower bound), plus a STATUS REPORT (essential self-adjointness open in 2012).
published_hypotheses: P1 quadratic operators normal-ordered with respect to the Minkowski vacuum (4D Minkowski spacetime; fields studied: massless scalar phi^2, phi-dot^2, rho_S; electromagnetic E^2, rho_EM)

P2 smearing function real-valued (so the smeared operator is symmetric); the paper's own computations use Lorentzian time-averaging along the time axis at a fixed spatial point, but the Sec. I remark is stated for smeared normal-ordered operators generally

P3 the operator is defined in the first instance only as a symmetric operator on 'a dense domain' (domain not specified in Sec. I; p. 10 works with 'states obtained from the vacuum by applying polynomials of smeared fields')
P4 the operator is bounded from below 'on account of quantum inequalities' (Sect. II A, Eq. (1): time-sampled QI, -C/tau^d); this semiboundedness is the input to Friedrichs
P5 the Friedrichs extension (Reed-Simon II Thm X.23) is CHOSEN ('It is this operator that we have in mind'); its lower bound equals the sharpest QI bound over the domain
P6 essential self-adjointness 'nontrivial and not fully resolved'; Sanders 1010.3978 'not, however, immediately applicable'
P7 distinct self-adjoint extensions, if any, share the same vacuum moments (the distributions may still differ: moment indeterminacy is discussed separately, Secs. I, IV, VIII A)
hypothesis_drift: ADDED (domain fixed): noise.py:157-158 realises A_tau as the Friedrichs extension 'on Hadamard vectors'; FFR p. 2 say only 'a dense domain'. The Friedrichs extension depends on the initial domain, so the tree has fixed an object FFR leave open. The lower bound used by C1 is robust to this choice: the Friedrichs lower bound equals inf of <psi,A psi>/||psi||^2 over the chosen domain, so it is >= -C/tau^4 on ANY dense linear domain on every vector of which Fewster 1208.5399 bound (3) holds. Unstated here: that the chosen 'Hadamard vectors' form a dense linear subspace on which A_tau is symmetric (Sanders 1010.3978 uses the Wightman domain D_omega, which consists of such vectors). A naming gap, not an error.

WIDENED (field and sampler class), harmless for this entry: noise.py:154 H1 takes m >= 0 and noise.py:163-165 H4 a compactly supported sampler root g in W^{2,2}; FFR compute with massless fields and a Lorentzian. The Sec. I remark itself is functional analysis valid for any semibounded symmetric operator, and semiboundedness for the tree's class is carried by Fewster 1208.5399 (H4), not by FFR; so the widening is not drift in what FFR Sec. I supports.

ADDED (tree's own claim, not in FFR): noise.py:160-162 and ledger.py:589-590, specthm.py:2239 'a different self-adjoint extension of a semibounded operator need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound'. FFR do not say this; it is a correct general fact (the Friedrichs extension is the largest semibounded extension in form order; other extensions can have lower bound strictly below). CONFIRMED on a closed-form model in the re-derivation (Robin extension of -d^2/dx^2 on the half-line: eigenvalue -kappa^2 below the Friedrichs bound 0).

DROPPED (FFR's P7, in neither direction's favour decisively): the tree does not carry FFR's sentence that distinct extensions share the vacuum moments. Carrying it would narrow H3's consequence for the VACUUM distribution only: if the vacuum moment problem were Hamburger-determinate, every extension would give the same vacuum distribution, supported in [-C/tau^4, oo), and H3 would not be needed for the vacuum statement. FFR p. 20 say 'on balance our expectation is that the problem is indeed indeterminate', and the re-derivation (C5) exhibits equal moments with different supports, so H3 stays load-bearing as the tree says. C1 is stated for every state (noise.py:28-35), where P7 does not apply at all.

NO DRIFT in status: noise.py:160 quotes 'not fully resolved' verbatim (source p. 2), and noise.py:324 labels H3 'ASSUMED, load-bearing' -- matching FFR's own 'It is this operator that we have in mind' (a choice, not a theorem). The tree does not upgrade the choice to a theorem.

data_at_publication.quantity: status of essential self-adjointness of the smeared normal-ordered quadratic operator the tree calls A_tau (4D free scalar energy density, smeared along a timelike worldline)
data_at_publication.value_then: 2012: 'nontrivial and not fully resolved' (FFR p. 2); Sanders 1010.3978 'not immediately applicable'
data_at_publication.value_now: Sanders 1010.3978v3 (Apr 2012, READ): ESA on the Wightman domain proved for the Wick square WITHOUT derivatives smeared with a SPACETIME test function in class S (finite sums of squares of real test functions), any quasi-free Hadamard state, any globally hyperbolic spacetime, d >= 2 (Thm 5.8); WITH derivatives only conditional on ESA of the one-particle compression (Thm 5.4), and a distinguished monotone-limit extension (Thm 5.3). A worldline-smeared (delta in space) derivative Wick square -- the tree's A_tau -- is covered by none of these. Schiappacasse-Fewster-Ford 1711.09477 and Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (READ) do not resolve it: the former diagonalises a finite-mode truncation in a sphere, the latter is 2D CFT, where T(f) is self-adjoint and whose Sec. 5 says the methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'. One discover_papers search found no later resolution; absence of a found paper is not proof of absence.
data_at_publication.moves_conclusion: No. H3 is ASSUMED either way. A future ESA proof for A_tau would DISCHARGE H3 (Friedrichs becomes the unique self-adjoint extension); a proof of non-ESA would leave H3 a choice, as the tree already carries it. No numerical datum enters this entry.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (9 checks, exit 0). The QFT operator is not finite, so the two functional-analytic claims are exercised on the closed-form model A = -d^2/dx^2 on C_c^inf(0,oo): C1 form bound 0 (sympy); C2 dilated Rayleigh quotient = 1/(19 s^2) -> 0+ (Friedrichs=Dirichlet lower bound = form bound, not attained); C3 Robin boundary form vanishes (a symmetric extension of A); C4 Robin eigenvector sqrt(2)e^{-x}, eigenvalue -1 < 0 = Friedrichs bound -- the tree's 'a different self-adjoint extension ... need not keep the Friedrichs lower bound' CONFIRMED; C5 for phi = x^10 e^{-x}, moments m_0..m_4 computed from the Dirichlet (sine) and Robin (atom + continuum) spectral resolutions agree with <phi, A^n phi> to 30 digits, yet the Robin measure has mass 6.279e6 (of ||phi||^2 = 1.160e12) at -1, below the Friedrichs bound -- FFR's P7 (shared moments) CONFIRMED and shown NOT to fix the support, which is why H3 is load-bearing. Not checked: that the QFT A_tau is or is not essentially self-adjoint (open at source and in the later literature read); Reed-Simon Thm X.23 itself (NAMED-NOT-READ; exercised on the model only).

later_literature.ref: K. Sanders, arXiv:1010.3978v3 (J. Math. Phys. 53, 042502 (2012)) -- FFR's ref. [18]
later_literature.what: Proves ESA of :phi^2:(f) on the Wightman domain for f in class S (sums of squares of real SPACETIME test functions) in every quasi-free Hadamard representation (Thm 5.8); for Wick squares with derivatives (stress-tensor components) only if the one-particle compression is ESA (Thm 5.4); gives a distinguished self-adjoint extension as a monotone strong-resolvent limit (Thm 5.3); notes the Wick square is semibounded for f in S so a Friedrichs extension exists (p. 10). Narrows FFR's open question to derivative Wick squares and non-S / worldline smearings -- the tree's A_tau remains in the open part.

later_literature.ref: E.D. Schiappacasse, C.J. Fewster, L.H. Ford, arXiv:1711.09477 (Phys. Rev. D 97, 025013 (2018))
later_literature.what: Bogoliubov-diagonalises a finite-mode truncation of the time-averaged :phi-dot^2: in a sphere; there C_shift is the lowest eigenvalue and 'both ... the lower bound on its probability distribution' (p. 9). Lorentzian C_shift = -0.0593338 vs FFR's moment estimate -0.0236, both inside the Fewster-Eveson bound -27/128 (p. 20). A finite truncation has no extension ambiguity, so it neither tests nor discharges H3.

In 2D unitary positive-energy CFT the smeared stress tensor is self-adjoint on D(L_0) with common core the intersection of D(L_0^k) (pp. 3, 6), and the infimum of the vacuum distribution's support equals the optimal QEI 'on general grounds' (p. 3, Eq. (1.5); checked for new families, Eq. (4.34)). Confirms the Friedrichs/QEI-bound identification where ESA holds; Sec. 5: methods have 'no straightforward generalization ... to higher spacetime dimensions'.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this entry. There is no measured datum in it: FFR's Sec. I is a choice of self-adjoint realisation plus a functional-analytic theorem plus a status report. What FFR lacked in 2012 was a MATHEMATICAL result -- a proof or disproof of essential self-adjointness for 4D smeared normal-ordered operators with derivatives under timelike smearing. The later literature read here does not supply it: Sanders (same year) covers :phi^2: with spacetime class-S smearing only; 1711.09477 and 1805.04281 do not reach the 4D worldline-smeared energy density. Evidence either way: (for) nothing found refutes FFR's statement or the tree's use; the Friedrichs lower-bound = form-bound identity and the tree's added 'need not keep the bound' both check on a closed-form model; (against M's suspicion applying here) FFR's statement is carefully hedged -- it claims no ESA, names the choice, and flags the gap -- so there is nothing 'inaccurate, incomplete or wrong' to find in it at the level the tree uses. Having the missing result would change the TREE's status line (H3 ASSUMED -> discharged if ESA holds), not FFR's conclusion or C1's bound for the Friedrichs extension.
grade_evidence: (1) Statement READ at source, p. 2: FFR mean the Friedrichs extension, whose lower bound is the sharpest QI bound, and say ESA is 'nontrivial and not fully resolved' -- noise.py:157-162 and :324 reproduce both, the quote verbatim, and carry the choice as 'ASSUMED, load-bearing', not as a theorem. (2) Drifts: the domain 'Hadamard vectors' is added (noise.py:158) where FFR say 'a dense domain'; the lower bound C1 uses is domain-robust provided the QEI holds on each domain vector (named gap: that the domain is a dense linear subspace); the field/sampler widening is not carried by this entry; the tree's added 'other extensions need not keep the bound' is true; FFR's shared-moments sentence is dropped, and carrying it would not remove H3's load (C5). (3) Re-derivation: 9/9 PASS on the closed-form model, agreeing with FFR and with the tree's addition. (4) No datum enters; the only moved item (Sanders 2012 v3) narrows the open ESA question without reaching the tree's operator, so it does not move the conclusion. The ESA question itself remains OPEN, and the tree already treats it so.
what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree's domain 'Hadamard vectors' were shown not to be a dense linear subspace on which A_tau is symmetric and Fewster's bound (3) holds for every vector (then the Friedrichs extension named in H3 would be ill-posed as written, though repairable on the Wightman domain). A published proof that the worldline-smeared 4D energy density is essentially self-adjoint would not lower the grade; it would discharge H3 (the tree should then retire 'ASSUMED'). A published proof of NON-essential-self-adjointness together with Hamburger indeterminacy of the relevant moments would sharpen D22's H3 caveat into a live alternative, still not a WRONG for FFR's statement, which claims neither. A reading of Reed-Simon II Thm X.23 contradicting 'lower bound of the Friedrichs extension = form bound' would reopen (1); the model check (C2, C4) agrees with it.
